title: Particle-Number-Preserving Quantum Signal Processing for Thermal Properties: Canonical-Ensemble Estimation and Grand-Canonical Reconstruction
authors: Taehee Ko, Sungbin Lim, Sangkook Choi
abstract: We develop an end-to-end framework for estimating canonical thermal properties of particle-number-conserving second-quantized Hamiltonians using quantum simulations. The framework integrates initial state preparation with mixed Dicke states, particle-number-preserving Trotterized simulation, and generalized quantum signal processing to estimate canonical partition functions and observables. Building on this canonical scheme, we introduce a grand-canonical reconstruction scheme in which the same quantum measurement data can be reused for arbitrary chemical potentials through classical reweighting, thereby avoiding repeated quantum circuit executions as the chemical potential is varied. We prove the existence of system-size-independent temperature regimes in which both the canonical and reconstructed grand-canonical schemes have lower asymptotic time complexity than classical Lanczos methods, up to polynomial factors, for physically relevant Hamiltonians. We numerically validate our theoretical results for the two-dimensional Hubbard model in both weak- and intermediate-coupling regimes.
summary: This paper presents a novel quantum algorithm using Quantum Signal Processing to estimate thermal properties for quantum systems, specifically focusing on particle-number-conserving Hamiltonians. It introduces a powerful grand-canonical reconstruction technique that reuses quantum measurement data when varying the chemical potential. The work proves that this quantum approach can achieve better scaling than classical methods for calculating key thermodynamic observables.
main_problem: Developing an efficient, end-to-end quantum framework to estimate canonical and grand-canonical thermal properties for particle-number-conserving quantum systems.
main_result: The proposed quantum algorithms achieve lower asymptotic time complexity than classical Lanczos methods in system-size-independent temperature regimes, and the grand-canonical reconstruction avoids re-running quantum circuits when varying the chemical potential.
method: The framework uses Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) combined with particle-number-preserving Trotterized quantum simulations to estimate thermal expectation values and partition functions.
model_or_system: The study applies to second-quantized Hamiltonians, exemplified by the two-dimensional Hubbard model, which describes interacting lattice electronic systems.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on constructing Trotter circuits that preserve particle number and uses classical reweighting techniques for grand-canonical reconstruction.

Theoretical proofs establish complexity bounds compared to classical methods, and the results are numerically validated on the 2D Hubbard model.
why_interesting: It provides a quantum computational pathway to calculate fundamental thermodynamic quantities (like partition functions) that are central to condensed matter physics, offering potential speedups over established classical numerical techniques.
